record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let X be a smooth contractible affine complex surface of log-general type. Must X contain a once-punctured curve, and if it does, can it contain only finitely many such curves?

evidence.quote: QUESTION. Does X contain any once-punctured curve ? Does it contain only a ﬁnite number of such curves ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth contractible affine complex algebraic surface of log-general type, i.e. its logarithmic Kodaira dimension $\bar\kappa(X)$ equals $2$. (Equivalently, for a smooth projective completion $\overline{X}$ of $X$ with simple normal crossing boundary divisor $D=\overline{X}\setminus X$, the divisor $K_{\overline{X}}+D$ is big.) A once-punctured curve on $X$ is a closed algebraic curve $C\subset X$ such that the normalization of $C$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{A}^1\setminus\{0\}=\mathbb{C}^*$ (a smooth rational curve with exactly one puncture).

(a) Must such an $X$ contain at least one once-punctured curve?

(b) If $X$ contains some once-punctured curves, can the set of once-punctured curves on $X$ be infinite, or must it always be finite?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return a definitive resolution of the question concerning the existence and finiteness of once-punctured curves on smooth contractible affine complex surfaces of log-general type. Related work on contractible affine surfaces and their logarithmic Kodaira dimensions exists, but no source clearly settles this specific question.
